protocol.hipengine: Create one cached-only resident max-512 session, run an initialization prefill, reset, warm the identical prefill five seconds before the target, reset, and collect only the final synchronized 512-token prefill in a bounded rocprof collection window.
protocol.llamacpp: llama-bench -r 1 emits one warmup and one measured pp512 pass. The measured pass is isolated after the first lm-head terminator, reproducing the established 2259-dispatch extraction rule.
protocol.timing_note: Profiler wall and kernel-family values are diagnostic. The prospectively frozen non-profiled 1+3 throughput floor remains the performance verdict. Cross-engine family names are structural crosswalks rather than claims of identical fused math.

conclusion: The production route remains GDN-bound, but GPF-9C removes that first-order bottleneck: its peer recurrence is only 0.612 ms slower than llama.cpp and the full named GDN chain only 3.689 ms slower. The GPF-9C and llama.cpp summed GPU work is nearly equal (207.253 versus 203.301 ms). The decisive short-prompt residual is queue starvation: hipEngine leaves 28.061 ms idle between kernels versus 8.935 ms for llama.cpp, a 19.126 ms excess and 82.9% of the trace-span delta, despite launching 614 fewer kernels. The largest kernel-family excess is dense Q8 (+20.825 ms), followed by convolution (+8.148 ms), while selected Q4/Q5 (-21.819 ms) and remaining layout/post-ops (-9.403 ms) compensate. Further GDN recurrence algebra is not the measured 512 target. The next retained work should attack copy-boundary queue bubbles first and a genuinely new dense-Q8 path second; do not retune selected Q4/Q5, full attention, or generic launch count.
